text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- The youth wings of the Social Democrats, Liberals, Conservatives, Radical Liberals and Centre Democrats agree that state pensions should be abolished and replaced by personal pension savings and that all Danes receiving state benefits should be put to work to bring down state debts. The youngsters criticise parliament for not putting state debt on the political agenda.

--- The number of stowaways on Danish ships is now estimated at about 100 a year compared to only ten a few years ago. The stowaways are mainly Romanians who use Danish ships to get to the U.S.A, but other Eastern Europeans also sneak on board Danish ships.

--- A survey made by the daily newspaper Jyllands Posten of 14 local authorities shows that they are ready to grant more than 500 million crowns in total, to raise standards at Danish hospitals. The government and parliament are expected to grant the same amount of money to healthcare in next year's state budget.

--- An increasing number of women now want to become farmers and now make up almost one third of people being admitted to agricultural schools. According to the Danish Agricultural Organisation, changing roles for men and women have contributed to women's increasing interest in farming.

--- Economics minister, Marianne Jelved, thinks that the EU currency will be used by all Danes in a few years in spite of Denmark's not participating in the European Monetary Union. The minister thinks that a referendum will replace the crown by the euro or that the euro will be introduced as a parallel currency. 64 percent of all Danish business leaders do not think that Denmark will get the euro when it is introduced in 1999, but expect Denmark to join later on.
